name: Project Copper
owner: Founder plans to step back; engineering and service leads expected to remain
niche: Integrated communications, access-control hardware, and facility system software for institutional and commercial buildings
moat: Seller claims integration expertise, installed-system knowledge, and service relationships. Verify vendor certifications, license transfer rights, and customer switching costs.
culture: Engineering-lead retention and field-service coverage remain unverified.
equity: Seller open to a minority rollover; terms unconfirmed.
summary: A fictional systems integrator combining communications and access-control hardware, third-party software configuration, installation, and ongoing support. The sample financials fit the published ranges; the quality of recurring service revenue still needs proof.
risks: Validate the sample revenue mix: 44% hardware and installation, 32% contracted maintenance, and 24% managed monitoring and software support. Separate contracted revenue from repeat projects.
Review manufacturer and software-reseller agreements, certification renewals, and change-of-control provisions. This is an integrator, not assumed proprietary SaaS.
Reconcile EBITDA and net income; test project cost estimates, work in progress, warranty reserves, and cash collection milestones.
Verify backlog conversion and cancellation rights. Backlog is not recurring revenue.
Confirm key-engineer retention, administrator access controls, remote-support security, and customer handover plans.
next: Schedule an owner and engineering-lead call. Request service contracts, the project-margin ledger, backlog aging, vendor agreements, and a management retention plan.

name: Project Arroyo
owner: Owner wants to step back; handover timing not provided
niche: Connected meters, building-control integrations, and energy dashboards for commercial facilities
moat: Seller claims integration expertise; verify proprietary code ownership versus third-party resale.
culture: Owner appears to lead sales; management depth is unknown.
summary: Revenue and EBITDA fit, but missing net income prevents a margin decision. Customer concentration adds a separate diligence concern.
risks: Obtain net income and margin by hardware, integration services, and software.
Review the largest customer contract, representing 34% of revenue.
Confirm software licensing, key integrator retention, and support obligations.
next: Request the missing financials and transition plan before advancing the deal.

name: Project Mesa
owner: Founder seeks a short exit with limited ongoing involvement
niche: Project-based audiovisual hardware installations with limited managed-service revenue
moat: Hardware resale and installation, with limited evidence of proprietary software or recurring contracts.
culture: Key estimator and project leads have no documented retention plan.
equity: Seller requests a full cash exit.
summary: The company fits the size ranges, but the 7% net margin is below the published threshold. Low recurring revenue and a two-month handover weaken the fit.
risks: Most revenue depends on new hardware installations rather than subscriptions.
Net margin falls below the published requirement.
The seller’s transition is shorter than SRC’s stated range.
next: Pass under this demonstration’s rules. Revisit only if verified economics or the mandate change.
